data.content_ref: inline:Target incorrectly identifies anthropogenic heat flux as the dominant single mechanism explaining why the nocturnal UHI gap is larger in some cities than others. The target omits the canonical mechanism for the first part of the question (why cities are warmer on clear, calm nights) and misattributes the cross-city modulator. The literature (Oke 1982, 1988) shows that the dominant single mechanism best explaining cross-city variation in nocturnal UHI under clear, calm conditions is urban geometry/sky view factor (the ability of urban surfaces to radiatively cool to the sky), not anthropogenic heat. A classic counterexample is cities with dense street canyons and low sky view factors exhibiting large nocturnal UHI with negligible anthropogenic heat input, demonstrating that anthropogenic heat is not the dominant modulator.
